assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups (plants, animals, microorganisms). It only describes a single organism, euglena, without placing it in a classification group or comparing characteristics.

copy.en:
How does a euglena find sunlight?

A euglena has a red eyespot that senses light, then swims toward the sun using its long tail (flagellum) to make food by photosynthesis!
copy.tl:
Paano nakikita ng euglena ang liwanag?

May pulang eyespot ang euglena na nakakaramdam kung saan may liwanag, tapos lumalangoy ito papunta sa araw gamit ang mahabang buntot (flagellum) para makagawa ng pagkain sa photosynthesis!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkita sa euglena sa kahayag?

Adunay pula nga eyespot ang euglena nga makabati kon asa ang kahayag, dayon molangoy kini paingon sa adlaw gamit ang taas nga ikog (flagellum) aron makahimo og pagkaon sa photosynthesis!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A slipper-shaped micro-organism living in pond water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a paramecium as a micro-organism but does not state that it is unicellular or contrast it with multicellular organisms. It does not directly teach the recognition of single-celled vs. many-celled organisms.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A slipper-shaped micro-organism living in pond water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of a micro-organism but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups (plants, animals, microorganisms). It does not support the classification skill required by the competency.

copy.en:
What is a paramecium?

A slipper-shaped micro-organism living in pond water that moves by waving tiny hairs called cilia.
copy.tl:
Ano ang paramecium?

Isang mikroorganismo sa tubig-lawa na hugis-sapatos at gumagalaw gamit ang maliliit na buhok-buhok na tinatawag na cilia.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang paramecium?

Usa ka mikroorganismo sa tubig-danaw nga porma og sapatos ug naglihok gamit ang gagmay nga balahibo nga gitawag cilia.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a porcupine raises its quills and rattles them loudly — a clear warning telling enemies to back off
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not an example of mimicry or camouflage as animals changed to better suit their environment.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce

assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

copy.en: Before it fights, a porcupine raises its quills and rattles them loudly — a clear warning telling enemies to back off.
copy.tl: Bago lumaban, itinitindig ng porcupine ang mga tinik nito at nagpapakalansing bilang babala sa kalaban na lumayo.
copy.bis: Sa dili pa makig-away, ipatindog sa porcupine ang iyang tunok ug ipakalansing kini isip pasidaan sa kaaway nga mopahawa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is made by grinding burned mixed rock into a very fine powder.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card states what Portland cement is and how it is made (grinding burned rock), but it does not describe how changes in solid materials make them useful through shaping, pressing, hammering, joining, or cutting. Grinding is not one of the listed changes, and no usefulness is explained.

copy.en:
What is the most common type of cement?

It is called Portland cement! It is made by grinding burned mixed rock into a very fine powder.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakakaraniwang uri ng semento?

Ito ay tinatawag na Portland cement! Gawa ito sa pinaghalong sinunog na bato na giniling na pinong-pino.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang labing komon nga matang sa semento?

Gitawag kini nga Portland cement! Hinimo kini pinaagi sa paggaling sa sinunog nga sagol nga bato ngadto sa pino kaayo nga pulbos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: helps your muscles and nerves work properly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions muscles and nerves but only states that potassium helps them work properly. It does not describe how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems work, which is the required action of the competency.

copy.en: Potassium, found in bananas and sweet potato, helps your muscles and nerves work properly.
copy.tl: Ang potasyum, na makukuha sa saging at kamote, ay tumutulong sa tamang paggana ng mga kalamnan at nerbiyo.
copy.bis: Ang potasyum, makuha sa saging ug kamote, motabang sa hustong paglihok sa mga kaunuran ug nerbiyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Prairie dogs munch on grass, plants, and seeds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states what prairie dogs eat but does not name the herbivore/carnivore/omnivore groups or provide any grouping activity or comparison across animals. It is a single dietary fact, not instruction that supports the skill of grouping animals by food type.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Prairie dogs munch on grass, plants, and seeds they find right near their burrows.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a habitat (near burrows) and an animal, but it does not make a list or table of animals and plants in a named habitat. The format-required list/table is absent, so it cannot directly support G4-L-4.

copy.en: Prairie dogs munch on grass, plants, and seeds they find right near their burrows.
copy.tl: Kumakain ang mga prairie dog ng damo, halaman, at buto na natatagpuan nila malapit sa kanilang lungga.
copy.bis: Mokaon ang mga prairie dog og sagbot, tanom, ug liso nga makit-an nila duol sa ilang lungib.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you must test your guess with materials and steps
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the steps of a simple science investigation (What is the problem? What materials do you need? What do you need to do? What have you found out/learned?)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that guesses must be tested with materials and steps, but it does not describe the actual steps of a simple science investigation (problem, materials, procedure, findings). It only encourages testing over arguing, which is related to the scientific method but does not directly teach the competency.

copy.en: You can guess what will happen, but you must test your guess with materials and steps, not just by arguing!
copy.tl: Pwede kang manghula, pero kailangan mong subukan ang hula gamit ang materyales at hakbang, hindi sa pamamagitan ng pagtatalo!
copy.bis: Pwede ka manghula, pero kinahanglan nimo sulayan ang hula gamit ang materyales ug lakang, dili sa pag-away!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: their tiny tips squeeze all the force into a small area, creating huge pressure that pierces skin easily
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate through guided investigation the advantages and limitations of simple machines, such as inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses force concentration and pressure from sharp objects, but does not mention simple machines, wedges, or guided investigation of advantages/limitations. It is only tangentially related to the wedge concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: their tiny tips squeeze all the force into a small area, creating huge pressure that pierces skin easily
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions force and pressure but does not address forces acting between objects or how forces can be measured. It provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Sharp things like nails and knives are dangerous because their tiny tips squeeze all the force into a small area, creating huge pressure that pierces skin easily!
copy.tl: Mapanganib ang mga matalas na bagay tulad ng pako at kutsilyo dahil pinipiga ng maliit na dulo ang lahat ng puwersa sa isang maliit na lugar, na gumagawa ng malaking presyon na madaling tumagos sa balat!
copy.bis: Delikado ang mga matalas nga butang sama sa pako ug kutsilyo tungod kay ang gamay nga tumoy nagpugos sa tanan nga puwersa sa gamay nga lugar, naghimo og dako nga presyon nga dali nga mosulod sa panit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A needle pierces easily because its sharp tip puts all the force onto one tiny point, creating very high pressure!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate through guided investigation the advantages and limitations of simple machines, such as inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains pressure concentration at a sharp point, which is conceptually related to how a wedge concentrates force, but it does not discuss simple machines, their advantages/limitations, or any of the named examples (inclined planes, wedges, levers, pulleys). It provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: A needle pierces easily because its sharp tip puts all the force onto one tiny point, creating very high pressure!
copy.tl: Madaling tumusok ang karayom dahil ang talim nitong dulo ay naglalagay ng buong puwersa sa isang maliit na punto, kaya napakataas ng presyon!
copy.bis: Sayon motusok ang dagom kay ang talinis niini nga tumoy nagbutang sa tibuok puwersa sa usa ka gamay nga punto, mao nga taas kaayo ang presyur!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The sharp tip concentrates force into a very tiny area
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses force and pressure but does not address identifying that forces act between objects or that forces can be measured, which is the core of G7-F-1.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The sharp tip concentrates force into a very tiny area
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: determine how forces can change the shape of objects such as when they are pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, or squeezed
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about pressure from a concentrated force, not about forces changing the shape of objects through pushing, pulling, stretching, bending, twisting, or squeezing as required by G4-F-6.

copy.en:
Why does a sharp nail easily pierce wood or a wall?

The sharp tip concentrates force into a very tiny area, creating very high pressure that drives the nail in!
copy.tl:
Bakit madaling tumagos ang matalas na pako sa kahoy o pader?

Nagtitipon ang matalas na dulo ng puwersa sa napakaliit na lawak, gumagawa ng napakataas na presyon para tumagos!
copy.bis:
Nganong sayon mosulod ang matalas nga pako sa kahoy o dingding?

Nagtipon ang matalas nga tumoy sa puwersa ngadto sa napakagamay nga lawak, naghimo og napakataas nga presyon nga nagmaneho sa pako!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: atmospheric pressure outside holds it in place
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a suction cup via air pressure, not by identifying balanced or unbalanced forces as defined in the competency (e.g., box resting, constant velocity, freely falling fruit). It does not teach the balanced/unbalanced force concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: atmospheric pressure outside holds it in place
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions atmospheric pressure as a force but does not address that forces act between objects or that they can be measured. It is about air pressure, not the general concept of forces and their measurement.

copy.en: Suction cups for phone holders work because of air pressure! Pressing it on glass squeezes air out, and atmospheric pressure outside holds it in place.
copy.tl: Gumagana ang suction cup ng phone holder dahil sa air pressure! Kapag pinindot sa salamin, lumalabas ang hangin, at atmospheric pressure sa labas ang humahawak nito.
copy.bis: Naggana ang suction cup sa phone holder tungod sa air pressure! Kung ipilit sa salamin, mogawas ang hangin, ug ang atmospheric pressure sa gawas ang mihawak niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The three primary colors of light are red, green, and blue!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that red, green, and blue are the primary colors of light. It does not compare wavelengths or frequencies of different electromagnetic waves, nor does it mention radio waves, microwaves, infrared, ultraviolet, x-rays, or gamma radiation. This is only tangentially related to visible light within the EM spectrum.

copy.en: The three primary colors of light are red, green, and blue! These are the most important colors of light.
copy.tl: Ang tatlong pangunahing kulay ng liwanag ay pula, berde, at asul! Ito ang pinakamahalagang mga kulay ng liwanag.
copy.bis: Ang tulo ka batakang kolor sa kahayag mao ang pula, berde, ug asul! Kini ang pinakaimportante nga mga kolor sa kahayag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: He published them in a famous book called 'Principia' way back in the year 1687!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies Isaac Newton as a famous foreign scientist, but it focuses on the book and year of publication of his laws of motion, not on an invention. Laws of motion are not inventions, so the card does not directly support identifying a scientist and their invention/s.

copy.en:
Where did Isaac Newton publish his famous laws of motion?

He published them in a famous book called 'Principia' way back in the year 1687!
copy.tl:
Saan inilathala ni Isaac Newton ang kanyang mga sikat na batas ng galaw?

Inilathala niya ang mga ito sa isang sikat na aklat na tinatawag na 'Principia' noong taong 1687!
copy.bis:
Asa gipatik ni Isaac Newton ang iyang bantog nga mga balaod sa paglihok?

Gipatik niya kini sa usa ka bantog nga libro nga gitawag og 'Principia' niadtong tuig 1687!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it can keep running at about 88 kilometers per hour over long stretches
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a speed value (88 km/h) but does not explain the concept that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It provides an example of speed without teaching the definition or relationship between distance and time.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pronghorn is the fastest long-distance runner of all
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe or identify any outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) or their roles in movement and food gathering. It only states the pronghorn's running ability, which is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
What animal wins the long-distance race?

The pronghorn is the fastest long-distance runner of all — it can keep running at about 88 kilometers per hour over long stretches!
copy.tl:
Anong hayop ang panalo sa malayong takbuhan?

Ang pronghorn ang pinakamabilis na hayop sa malayong takbo — kaya nitong tumakbo nang halos 88 kilometro kada oras nang matagal!
copy.bis:
Unsang mananap ang modaog sa layo nga dagan?

Ang pronghorn mao ang pinakapaspas nga modagan sa layo — makadagan kini og halos 88 kilometro kada oras sa taas nga panahon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When solid materials are mixed with other solids, their size, shape, and color usually stay the same.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses mixing solid materials and their unchanged properties. It does not mention solutions, solutes, or solvents, so it provides no support for identifying the role of solute and solvent in a solution.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When solid materials are mixed with other solids, their size, shape, and color usually stay the same.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about mixing solids, which is a type of mixture, but it does not describe uniform vs non-uniform mixtures, nor does it give examples of solutions or suspensions. It only touches on the general topic of mixtures without addressing the specific competency.

copy.en: When solid materials are mixed with other solids, their size, shape, and color usually stay the same.
copy.tl: Kapag ang mga solid na materyal ay inihalo sa ibang solid, ang kanilang laki, hugis, at kulay ay karaniwang nananatiling pareho.
copy.bis: Kung ang mga solid nga materyal isagol sa laing solid, ang ilang gidak-on, porma, ug kolor kasagarang magpabilin nga pareho.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One job of the prostate is to make a fluid that mixes with sperm and helps them travel!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the female reproductive system as ovaries, uterus, and vagina and those of the male reproductive system as the prostate, testis, and penis and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the prostate's function, which is part of the male reproductive system content of G5-L-3. However, the competency explicitly requires identification from pictures and labeled diagrams, and this card is a text-only Q&A with no such representation. Therefore it does not directly support the competency as specified.

copy.en:
What is one important job of the prostate?

One job of the prostate is to make a fluid that mixes with sperm and helps them travel!
copy.tl:
Ano ang isang mahalagang trabaho ng prostate?

Isa sa trabaho ng prostate ay gumawa ng likido na hinaluan ng semilya para matulungan ang semilya na maglakbay!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang usa ka importante nga trabaho sa prostate?

Usa sa mga trabaho sa prostate mao ang paghimo ug likido nga gisagol sa semilya aron matabangan ang semilya nga molakaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They are super fragile and take ages to regrow! We must never touch or break them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about protecting fragile cave formations, which are non-living geological features. The competency G3-L-8 focuses on protecting and conserving the environment so that living things can survive. The card does not mention living things or their survival, so it only shares the general theme of conservation without directly supporting the stated skill.

copy.en:
Why shouldn't we touch cave formations?

They are super fragile and take ages to regrow! We must never touch or break them.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi natin dapat hawakan ang mga pormasyon sa kuweba?

Napakadurog po nila at napakatagal mabuo muli! Kaya hindi natin dapat basta-basta hawakan o sirain.
copy.bis:
Nganong dili nato dapat hikapon ang mga pormasyon sa langob?

Huyang kaayo sila ug dugay kaayong motubo pag-usab! Mao nga dili nato kini dapat hikapon o gub-on.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Meat, fish, and eggs give complete proteins with all the amino acids we need.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses protein completeness and amino acid content, not the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It is nutrition-specific and does not directly support identifying basic needs.

copy.en: Meat, fish, and eggs give complete proteins with all the amino acids we need. Plant proteins are usually missing one or two, but combining them fixes that.
copy.tl: Ang karne, isda, at itlog ay may kumpletong protina na may lahat ng kailangang amino acid. Kulang ng isa o dalawa ang protina mula sa halaman, pero maayos ito kapag pinagsama.
copy.bis: Ang karne, isda, ug itlog adunay kompleto nga protina nga adunay tanang gikinahanglan nga amino acid. Kulang og usa o duha ang protina gikan sa tanom, apan maayo kini kon pagasamahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water keeps seeping into a paramecium by osmosis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses osmoregulation in a paramecium but never states that a paramecium is a single-celled organism or contrasts unicellular with multicellular organisms. It does not directly support recognizing unicellular vs. multicellular organization.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a tiny contractile vacuole regularly pumps the extra water back out to keep it safe
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes water balance in a single-celled organism, which is a homeostatic process, but the competency specifically requires describing homeostasis as a state of balance among all body systems in humans with indicators such as body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure. The card gives no human body system or indicator, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
How does a paramecium avoid bursting?

Water keeps seeping into a paramecium by osmosis, but a tiny contractile vacuole regularly pumps the extra water back out to keep it safe.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi sumasabog ang paramecium?

Palaging pumapasok ang tubig sa paramecium dahil sa osmosis, pero regular itong pinipiga palabas ng contractile vacuole para hindi ito masaktan.
copy.bis:
Nganong dili mubuto ang paramecium?

Kanunay mosulod ang tubig sa paramecium tungod sa osmosis, apan regular kining gipagawas sa contractile vacuole aron dili kini maunsa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Proxima Centauri is our closest star neighbor, sitting about 4.2 light-years away from us!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the distance to Proxima Centauri, a star outside the solar system. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or give their features and composition, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Proxima Centauri is our closest star neighbor, sitting about 4.2 light-years away from us!
copy.tl: Ang Proxima Centauri ay nasa layong humigit-kumulang 4.2 light-years mula sa atin, kaya malayo pa ito!
copy.bis: Ang Proxima Centauri mga 4.2 ka light-years ang gilay-on gikan kanato, mao nga malayo pa kaayo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it's the poison inside it that can harm you if you eat it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions spines but does not describe outer body parts or their role in movement or food gathering. It focuses on the internal poison, not the structure or function of body parts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it's the poison inside it that can harm you if you eat it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a pufferfish's poison but does not describe any adaptation, mimicry, or camouflage, nor how the animal changed to suit its environment.

copy.en:
What's really dangerous about a pufferfish?

It's not mainly the pufferfish's spines that are dangerous — it's the poison inside it that can harm you if you eat it.
copy.tl:
Ano talaga ang delikado sa butete?

Hindi ang tinik ng butete ang pangunahing delikado — ang lason sa loob nito ang nakakasama kapag ito ay kinain.
copy.bis:
Unsa gyud ang delikado sa butete?

Dili ang tunok sa butete ang una-una nga peligroso — ang hilo sa sulod niini ang makadaot kon kan-on kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When in danger, a pufferfish gulps water and puffs into a spiky ball
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an immediate defensive behavior, not an example of how an animal has changed over time to better suit its environment as required by G5-L-9 (e.g., mimicry or camouflage). It shares the broad topic of animal survival/defense but does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When in danger, a pufferfish gulps water and puffs into a spiky ball
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card illustrates a response to danger, which is a behavior, but it does not describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) or explicitly teach that living things respond. It is only tangentially related to the competency.

copy.en: When in danger, a pufferfish gulps water and puffs into a spiky ball — hard to eat, and some kinds are even poisonous!
copy.tl: Kapag nasa panganib, sumisipsip ng tubig ang pufferfish at namumuo na parang bilog na puno ng tinik — mahirap kainin, at may mga uri pa na may lason!
copy.bis: Kon namiligro, ang pufferfish mosuyop og tubig ug modako nga sama sa bola nga puno og tunok — lisod kan-on, ug ang uban makahilo pa gani!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its poison can kill
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a poison (toxin) but does not describe chemical properties of materials such as burning, reacting, or degradability. The poison is a biological toxin, not a material whose chemical properties are described.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its poison can kill
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things in the environment, such as trash disposal, and burning household materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card warns about a harmful effect of eating pufferfish, but the competency focuses on changes in materials (e.g., trash disposal, burning household materials) being harmful. The card does not explain changes in materials or their harmful effects on living/non-living things in the environment.

copy.en: In the Philippines, people are told not to eat pufferfish — it's easy to clean it wrong, and its poison can kill.
copy.tl: Sa Pilipinas, pinapayuhan ang mga tao na huwag kumain ng butete — madaling magkamali sa paglilinis nito at nakamamatay ang lason.

Ang mapula-pulang kulay at bahagyang init ng Rafflesia ang umaakit sa mga langaw — para sa langaw, mukha at amoy itong patay na hayop, tamang lugar pagitlugan!

Nganong daghang langaw sa Rafflesia?

Ang pula nga kolor ug gamayng init sa Rafflesia mao ang nakadani sa mga langaw — para sa langaw, murag patay nga hayop kini, maayong dapit itlogan!

copy.bis: Ang ikaduhang bahaghari sa ibabaw sa una adunay baligtad nga kolor — violet sa gawas ug pula sa sulod — tungod kay ang suga midoble-talbog sa sulod sa patak sa ulan!

Do rainbows only appear when it rains?

Nope! You can see them in waterfall, fountain, or garden hose spray when the sun shines. You just need light and tiny water droplets!
copy.tl:
Sa ulan lang ba lumalabas ang bahaghari?

Hindi! Makikita mo rin sila sa tilamsik ng talon, fountain, o manggera kapag sinisikatan ng araw. Kailangan lang ng liwanag at maliliit na patak ng tubig!
copy.bis:
Sa ulan lang ba mogawas ang balangaw?

Dili! Makita pod nimo kini sa tinilamsik sa busay, tubod, o hose kung silawan sa adlaw. Kinahanglan lang og kahayag ug gagmay nga tulo sa tubig!

Maraming halaman sa understory ay may malalapad na dahon para mahuli ang kakaunting liwanag na nakakalusot mula sa itaas.

Ngano nga lapad ang dahon sa tanom sa understory?

Daghang tanom sa understory adunay malapad nga mga dahon aron makuha ang gamay nga kahayag nga makalusot gikan sa taas.
